questions.stem: The diagram shows an endothelial cell releasing several mediators (NO, EDHF, ET-1, PGI2) that act on adjacent vascular smooth muscle, each marked with a plus or minus sign for its effect on contraction. Which of these endothelium-derived mediators PROMOTES vascular smooth muscle contraction?

explanation.summary: Of the endothelial mediators shown, ET-1 is the only vasoconstrictor (marked +), acting to increase smooth muscle contraction. NO, EDHF, and PGI2 all cause relaxation (marked -). ET-1 is produced when big-endothelin is cleaved by endothelin-converting enzyme (ECE).
explanation.whyCorrect: Of the endothelial mediators shown, ET-1 is the only vasoconstrictor (marked +), acting to increase smooth muscle contraction. NO, EDHF, and PGI2 all cause relaxation (marked -). ET-1 is produced when big-endothelin is cleaved by endothelin-converting enzyme (ECE).

questions.stem: In this pathway, shear stress raises endothelial Ca2+, activating NO synthase; the NO then diffuses into smooth muscle. Through which second messenger does NO ultimately trigger smooth muscle relaxation?

explanation.summary: NO diffuses into the smooth muscle cell and activates soluble guanylate cyclase, converting GTP to cGMP. cGMP activates myosin-light-chain phosphatase (and lowers Ca2+ availability), dephosphorylating myosin and producing relaxation/vasodilation.
explanation.whyCorrect: NO diffuses into the smooth muscle cell and activates soluble guanylate cyclase, converting GTP to cGMP. cGMP activates myosin-light-chain phosphatase (and lowers Ca2+ availability), dephosphorylating myosin and producing relaxation/vasodilation.

questions.stem: These paired tracings compare epinephrine and norepinephrine infusions. With norepinephrine, arterial pressure rises sharply yet heart rate transiently DROPS below baseline. What best explains this fall in heart rate?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct blockade of L-type calcium channels in the SA node

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct beta-1 stimulation of the SA node by norepinephrine

explanation.summary: Norepinephrine strongly raises mean arterial pressure via alpha-1 vasoconstriction. The baroreceptor reflex responds to this pressure rise by increasing vagal tone, which slows the heart despite norepinephrine's direct beta-1 effect. Epinephrine raises pressure less (beta-2 vasodilation partly offsets it), so its net effect is a rise in heart rate.
explanation.whyCorrect: Norepinephrine strongly raises mean arterial pressure via alpha-1 vasoconstriction. The baroreceptor reflex responds to this pressure rise by increasing vagal tone, which slows the heart despite norepinephrine's direct beta-1 effect. Epinephrine raises pressure less (beta-2 vasodilation partly offsets it), so its net effect is a rise in heart rate.

questions.stem: Panel A shows blood flow staying nearly constant over a wide range of perfusion pressures (the autoregulatory range); panel B shows a vessel constricting when stretched and dilating when relaxed. Which intrinsic mechanism is chiefly responsible for keeping flow constant as pressure changes here?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sympathetic vasomotor tone from the medulla

choices.label: C
choices.text: The myogenic response of vascular smooth muscle

explanation.summary: The myogenic mechanism is intrinsic: increased perfusion pressure stretches vascular smooth muscle, which responds by contracting (raising resistance) to hold flow constant; decreased pressure produces relaxation. This keeps flow relatively stable across the autoregulatory range independent of nerves or circulating hormones.
explanation.whyCorrect: The myogenic mechanism is intrinsic: increased perfusion pressure stretches vascular smooth muscle, which responds by contracting (raising resistance) to hold flow constant; decreased pressure produces relaxation. This keeps flow relatively stable across the autoregulatory range independent of nerves or circulating hormones.

questions.stem: The left tracing shows tissue blood flow rising and staying elevated during a period of increased metabolism, and the right graph shows steady-state flow rising with metabolic activity. This matching of flow to metabolic demand is primarily mediated by what?

explanation.summary: This is active (functional) hyperemia: increased tissue metabolism generates vasodilator metabolites and lowers local PO2, relaxing arterioles so that blood flow rises to match metabolic demand. It is a local, metabolically driven mechanism, not a neural or systemic hormonal one.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is active (functional) hyperemia: increased tissue metabolism generates vasodilator metabolites and lowers local PO2, relaxing arterioles so that blood flow rises to match metabolic demand. It is a local, metabolically driven mechanism, not a neural or systemic hormonal one.

questions.stem: This tracing shows flow held at zero (an arterial occlusion) followed, upon release, by a transient overshoot in flow above baseline. What primarily drives this post-occlusion overshoot?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Endothelin-1 release from the reperfused endothelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Accumulated vasodilator metabolites and tissue hypoxia

choices.label: C
choices.text: The myogenic response to the sudden pressure rise

choices.label: D
choices.text: A surge of circulating catecholamines on reperfusion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reflex sympathetic withdrawal triggered by cuff release

explanation.summary: During the no-flow period, vasodilator metabolites accumulate and PO2 falls, so the arterioles dilate maximally. When flow is restored, the low-resistance dilated vessels allow an excess (overshoot) flow until the metabolites wash out. This is reactive hyperemia, proportional to the duration of occlusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: During the no-flow period, vasodilator metabolites accumulate and PO2 falls, so the arterioles dilate maximally. When flow is restored, the low-resistance dilated vessels allow an excess (overshoot) flow until the metabolites wash out. This is reactive hyperemia, proportional to the duration of occlusion.

questions.stem: The schematic shows cellular metabolism lowering local PO2 and releasing substances (CO2, H+, adenosine, K+, decreased ATP) that relax the nearby arteriole. What is the physiologic purpose of the mechanism depicted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To buffer systemic arterial blood pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text: To promote thrombus formation in low-flow regions

choices.label: C
choices.text: To increase systemic vascular resistance during exercise

choices.label: D
choices.text: To trigger platelet aggregation at sites of injury

choices.label: E
choices.text: To match local blood flow to the metabolic demand of the tissue

explanation.summary: This is the metabolic theory of local flow control: active tissue consumes O2 and produces vasodilator metabolites (adenosine, CO2, H+, K+) with falling PO2, dilating local arterioles so blood flow increases in proportion to metabolic need (active hyperemia).
explanation.whyCorrect: This is the metabolic theory of local flow control: active tissue consumes O2 and produces vasodilator metabolites (adenosine, CO2, H+, K+) with falling PO2, dilating local arterioles so blood flow increases in proportion to metabolic need (active hyperemia).
